articles.title: ‘Tiny bit of rain and the sewage comes’: Brighton swimmers vent fury at sea pollution
articles.summary: Checking for sewage spills has become as normal as checking the weather forecast, say swimmers on East Sussex beaches. South West Water has worst environmental record in England, analysis shows. “I’m furious,” says Jo Armstrong, 75, sitting on Brighton beach with her daughter and granddaughter.
body: Armstrong lives in Lewes, a town 8 miles from Brighton, and usually goes swimming in nearby Seaford in East Sussex every day. But over the past week the water there has been too polluted to swim. “Brighton beach was the only place that stayed clean,” she says.

In the week Friends of the Earth ranked the UK’s water companies for their environmental damage, and news of further sewage leaks emerged, the Guardian headed to Brighton beach to talk to swimmers. According to public data, a sewage alert was issued twice at the beach in August, and 158 alerts recorded overall in 2025.
“There’s a tiny bit of rain and then the sewage comes, I just don’t understand it. It’s extraordinary that we can’t have clean beaches,” says Armstrong.

This summer England has endured record-breaking heatwaves during which scores of people have spent time on beaches and rivers. In Brighton, the state of the country’s water is an issue on many people’s minds.

articles.title: I’ve got feelings for a teacher at my children’s school. What should I do? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: Crushes can feel freeing because they operate outside everyday life, but does that mean you should act on them? I’ve been married for 20 years and have two children. By most measures, our marriage is stable and successful.
body: They are married with children too. Nothing inappropriate has happened, and neither of us has acknowledged any romantic feelings. However, I cannot shake the sense that there may be a mutual connection.

I am struggling with what these feelings mean. Are they evidence that something is missing in my marriage, or simply the result of encountering someone new after years with the same partner? Is this a genuine connection that deserves attention, or a fantasy that has never been tested by real life?
Most importantly, what should I do next? I do n’t want to hurt my wife, my children, this person, or their family. Yet pretending these feelings do n’t exist has n’t made them disappear.

The first thing to address is your use of the pronoun “they”. This makes me wonder if it’s a man or a woman you’ve developed feelings for. If it’s the former, and you’ve lived as a heterosexual man thus far, and that’s what your wife believes, then you need to be really honest with yourself and then your wife about what this all means beyond the crush.
points: Crushes can feel freeing because they operate outside everyday life, but does that mean you should act on them?
I’ve been married for 20 years and have two children.
By most measures, our marriage is stable and successful.
Nothing inappropriate has happened, and neither of us has acknowledged any romantic feelings.

articles.title: Tuscany’s treasured islands: five to explore
articles.summary: Want to avoid the crowds in Florence and Siena? Escape to these islands, from lively Elba to tiny, car-free Giannutri. Scattered between the Tuscan coast and Corsica, the seven islands of the Tuscan archipelago offer a striking contrast to mainland Tuscany.
body: As Italy’s third-largest island, and with a year-round community, Elba is the archipelago’s main tourist hub, blending Napoleonic history with rugged landscapes, lively seaside towns and fine beaches. It is famous for Napoleon’s brief 1814 exile at the Palazzina dei Mulini, but its history runs much deeper, with 16th-century Medici fortifications to defend against pirate raids around the coast, and medieval hill towns, some standing on sites occupied since Roman times, inland.

Beach lovers tend to divide between the white-pebble coves of Sansone and Capo Bianco near the largest town, Portoferraio, in the north, and the golden sands of Fetovaia and Cavoli in the south-west beneath Monte Capanne. Marina di Campo on the south coast is a favourite for watersports, and windsurfing and sailing schools are popular in many resorts, from Procchio in the north to Lacona in the south.

Hikers can explore the 36-mile (58km) Grande Traversata Elbana, crossing the island from Cavo in the north-east to Pomonte or Patresi on the west coast, passing along mountain ridges and through traditional villages. Usually completed in three or four days, it’s best tackled in spring or autumn.

Escape to these islands, from lively Elba to tiny, car-free Giannutri.

articles.title: Make your bed – and be ruthless: 14 expert rules for a clean, healthy, happy home
articles.summary: Is your place crying out for some TLC? Housekeepers reveal how to keep it looking its best – and when it’s OK to let standards slip. Life is busy and there is only so much time to spend cleaning and tidying. What are the non-negotiables of a well-managed home?
body: There are four elements to a well-run home, according to Matt Church, AKA Mr Housekeeping, from Maldon in Essex. These are keeping the place “clean, tidy, decluttered and organised,” he says. “I call myself a housekeeper because it’s not just cleaning. Cleaning is one element, but some cleaners wouldn’t tidy, empty bins, make beds, put laundry away or organise cupboards. They are all jobs I get involved with.” People laugh about tidying before the cleaner comes, but they are different things entirely, Church says.

“When you take on somebody’s house, a lot of it at the beginning is about listening,” says Georgie Cutbill, who runs The Bruton Housekeeper, a household management service in Somerset. “People have very particular ideas about what they want, so you’ve got to get into their headspace.” Cutbill has found herself in all kinds of surprising scenarios, from organising parties involving miniature donkeys to sourcing Tadelakt [Moroccan lime-based plaster] specialists. “No two days are the same,” she says.
points: Housekeepers reveal how to keep it looking its best – and when it’s OK to let standards slip.

articles.title: Amidst Tears and Fanfare, Roger Federer Is Inducted Into The International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport
articles.summary: With a crowd of thousands there to witness history, Federer, long a member-in-waiting, makes it official.
body: It was never a case of “if”—only “when.” It came down to a gorgeous Saturday night in Newport, Rhode Island, as Roger Federer, along with former pro player and acclaimed sports broadcaster Mary Carillo, was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame (ITHF)—the sort of honor that anyone who had seen him play throughout his storied career knew awaited him, sooner rather than later.

Tennis fans turned out in record numbers to pay tribute to both Carillo and Federer, with hundreds witnessing the ceremony in the ITHF’s historical Horseshoe Court and thousands more gathered nearby on the grounds at an enormous watch party—the culmination of days of events at the Hall of Fame, including Friday night’s Fit For Fame Blazer Presentation Dinner, in which the newest honorees receive their custom Brooks Brothers blue blazers with the ITHF racket logo on the pocket.
points: With a crowd of thousands there to witness history, Federer, long a member-in-waiting, makes it official.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s First Daisy Chain Fields Festival Look Comes With a Feminist Message
articles.summary: The pop star kicked off the inaugural women-led festival with the announcement that they’ve raised $10 million for women-focused non-profits.
body: Olivia Rodrigo has kicked off her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Festival; today, in the Great Park in Irvine, California, sees the likes of Stevie Nicks, Karen O, Chappell Roan, Doechii, Mitski, the Breeders, Bikini Kill, Sarah McLachlan, and Garbage take to the stage. Woman-led, intergenerational, and broad in sound, the acts encapsulate Rodrigo’s progressive stance in pop. 100 percent of the net proceeds will go to 10 non-profit organizations including Baby2Baby, the Center for Reproductive Rights, and Planned Parenthood, with community-led workshops and activities on-site.

Before all that, Rodrigo held a press presentation to share that $10 million would be donated to the orgs, spanning reproductive rights, mental health, domestic violence, and maternal health. Her outfit was also imbued with a feminist message that met the moment.
points: The pop star kicked off the inaugural women-led festival with the announcement that they’ve raised $10 million for women-focused non-profits.

articles.title: Kendall Jenner’s Latest Accessory: Finn Jenner (-Elordi?)
articles.summary: Stepping out in LA after a jaunt to London, the model dressed mostly in The Row, with a miniature wire-haired dachshund peeking out from the Tori tote.
body: Kendall Jenner is a longtime disciple of The Row. Only Jennifer Lawrence and Zoë Kravitz could rival her covetable collection of minimalist handbags, hats, and ballet flats. But there’s a new (and very cute) addition to Kendall’s collection of accessories: more canine than Olsen line.

The model was photographed out and about in Los Angeles yesterday, carrying a wire-haired dachshund—his name is Finn—in her capacious Tori bag from—where else?—The Row. It’s not Finn’s first paparazzi sighting either: Jenner and boyfriend Jacob Elordi were captured playing with the dog earlier in the summer while on a trip in Malibu.

She also sported what’s probably an upcoming collaboration with Beats. (And possibly Justin Bieber’s SKYLRK line, given the lime green accents that are similar to the wired headphones Hailey Bieber was also spotted wearing on a pap walk.) The rest of the outfit was textbook Kendall Jenner: a cropped white Flore Flore t-shirt and white pull-on cotton Gala pants from The Row, a black knit tied low on her waist, and black sneakers.

articles.title: I Had A Private Tennis Lesson From Grand Slam Champion Stan Wawrinka Inside The Waldorf Astoria Ballroom
articles.summary: First, I saw Ben Shelton, Tommy Paul, Leylah Fernandez, and Maria Sakkari play an exhibition; then I took to the court myself with the former US Open champion.
body: All sorts of funny things happen in New York in the week leading up to the main draw of the US Open. For one? Courts appear where you’ve never seen them before. This year, Racquet magazine hosted various festivities at an annual pop-up court at the South Street Seaport; Wilson threw a tennis party to debut their new Defyer racquet at the private Town Tennis Club, tucked into a residential building on a leafy street off Sutton Place; and Serena Williams, Matteo Berrettini, Taylor Fritz, and Caroline Wozniacki played pickleball in the stately ballroom of the Lotte New York Palace Hotel across the street from St. Patrick’s Cathedral in midtown.

What began with mild trepidation on the part of the players—“I just hope I don’t shank a ball and smash a chandelier,” said Tommy Paul a few minutes before the cocktail hour kicked off—turned into a kind of triumphal arrival of, perhaps, a new Manhattan tradition. “Here’s hoping that this is just the first of many of these—and that, maybe, I even get invited back,” said Ben Shelton out on the court.
